claims.text: Catalytic activity in transition-metal catalysts is governed by the position of the d-band center.
Catalytic selectivity in transition-metal catalysts is governed by the position of the d-band center.
The d-band-center position determines the binding energy of key reaction intermediates.
Controlled alloying can shift the d-band center.
Applying lattice strain can shift the d-band center.
A shift in the d-band center changes the adsorption strength of reaction intermediates.
Changes in intermediate adsorption strength modulate catalytic reactivity and selectivity.
The surface d-band-center shift mediates the effect of catalyst modification on intermediate binding energies.
Moderate d-band-center shifts can optimize the balance between excessively strong and excessively weak adsorbate binding.
Optimized adsorbate binding enhances catalytic turnover rate.
Optimized adsorbate binding enhances catalytic selectivity.
Excessive d-band-center shifts can over-stabilize or under-bind adsorbates and thereby reduce catalytic performance.
Catalysts with a controlled, moderate d-band-center shift will exhibit higher reaction rates than an unmodified catalyst.
Catalysts with a controlled, moderate d-band-center shift will exhibit improved selectivity relative to an unmodified catalyst.
The hypothesis is expected to apply when intermediate binding energies are rate-determining and particle size, surface defects, and morphology are controlled.
The proposed mechanism is particularly applicable to electrocatalytic oxygen reduction and moderate-temperature CO oxidation.
